mode: Behavioral scenarios; expected outcomes are rubrics, not executed MCP results

evals.prompt: Build five ordered qualification questions mapped to attributes and move to Qualified on completion.
evals.expected_output: The skill verifies target stage/attribute IDs and allowed values, validates/simulates branches, applies with approval, reads back and verifies completion behavior without using an AI score shortcut.

evals.prompt: Lead answered A then corrected to C, but CRM still shows A.
evals.expected_output: The skill treats the latest explicit correction as authoritative subject to mapping validation, inspects trace/action persistence and repairs only through canonical lead/qualification tools.

evals.prompt: The AI text says 'you are qualified' but stage stayed New Lead.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not force the stage from text alone; it diagnoses required-answer evidence, completion contract, target stage and transition attempt first.

evals.prompt: A user refuses one required question. Mark them qualified because the other four answers are good.
evals.expected_output: The skill preserves the required-evidence contract, does not use majority-answer logic or refusal sentinels, and follows the configured refusal/handoff behavior.

evals.prompt: Update qualification and then overwrite the final Playbook with an older draft.
evals.expected_output: The skill orders changes to avoid losing generated/qualification-owned sections and requires a fresh full Playbook read before replacement.
